clue.text: A lake in Georgia for a carnival

indicators.note: the clue puts the first pieces in Georgia, so they go inside its abbreviation

parts.note: GA is the US postal abbreviation for the state of Georgia
L is the standard map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A trip to a Georgian lake for some festival fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a festive public celebration, much like a fair or fete.

clue.text: How a switch is said to stop a horse?

indicators.note: to switch things round is to change their order, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A riddle about how a riding crop is spoken of when reining in a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switch' looks like a riding whip, but it tells you to swap the letters of HOW A around.
explanation.definitionFit: The call riders give to make a horse halt is the classic stopping command.

clue.text: King and eccentric person, literally?

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
a nut is slang for a crazy or eccentric person

explanation.surface: A monarch with a screw loose, taken at face value.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'literally' as spelling out the letters: K and NUT side by side give the Danish king's name, and the word also once meant a showy dandy.
explanation.definitionFit: Knut is the Danish spelling of Canute, the king; it was also Edwardian slang for a foppish young man.

clue.text: Outpourings from Burns, say

definitions.meaning: flows or gushes of anything, like tears or words
in Scotland a burn is a small brook, so burns are examples of these watercourses

explanation.surface: Poetic effusions from Robert Burns, Scotland's national poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burns' looks like the poet Robert Burns, but it is the Scottish word for brooks.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are flows: gushes of words or feeling, and small brooks of running water.

clue.text: Warning to keep this deck structure

parts.note: golfers shout fore as a warning to anyone in the ball's path
a keep is the fortified tower of a fortress, so it stands for castle

explanation.surface: A caution to preserve a particular part of a ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keep' looks like a verb meaning preserve, but it is the noun for a fortified tower.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised forward part of a ship's upper deck is its forecastle, a structure built on the deck.

clue.text: Young feller in whom nothing was misrepresented

indicators.note: to misrepresent is to present wrongly, so these letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A boy so honest that nothing he said was ever twisted.
explanation.walkthrough: The legend says young George Washington chopped down a cherry tree and could not tell a lie, so he is the boy who 'felled' it and never misrepresented anything.
explanation.definitionFit: In the famous fable the future first US president, as a child, cut down a cherry tree with his hatchet.

clue.text: Scandal in Rye-toot is involved!

indicators.note: something involved is tangled up, so the letters of these words are jumbled

explanation.surface: An outcry about a scandal in the Sussex town of Rye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word but is part of the fodder: IN plus RYETOOT rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Notoriety is the fame of being known for something bad, the state a scandal brings.

clue.text: Meridian, whichever way you look at it

indicators.text: whichever way you look at it
indicators.note: the same word comes out whether read forwards or backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Midday looks the same from any angle.
explanation.definitionFit: The meridian is the sun's highest point, so midday is called meridian.

clue.text: Lost again, wandering, Browning suffered it in the spring

definitions.text: Browning suffered it in the spring

indicators.note: something wandering strays from its path, so these letters drift into a new order

explanation.surface: A lost traveller wanders again, much as the poet did one spring.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Browning's poem 'Home-Thoughts, from Abroad' begins 'Oh, to be in England / Now that April's there', a longing for home in spring.
explanation.definitionFit: Homesick longing for a place or time gone is what Browning's poem expresses.

clue.text: Flat isolated? Chaps will need a little time

parts.note: apart means separated from others, as isolated
chaps are men
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A lonely flat where the occupants are short of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' could be an adjective, but it is the British word for a set of rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat is the British word for an apartment, a set of rooms on one floor.

clue.text: Regret the French way?

definitions.meaning: to regret is to wish something undone
the French word for a street, a way in Paris

explanation.surface: Feeling sorry about how things are done in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the French way' looks like a manner of doing things; it is a street in French.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue is to be sorry for something; a rue is a French street.

clue.text: Slough outbuilding

definitions.meaning: to slough is to cast off, as a snake does its skin
a small hut in a garden or yard

explanation.surface: A garden hut in the Berkshire town of Slough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slough' looks like the English town west of London, but it is the verb for casting off.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake casts off its skin, and a garden hut is a small outbuilding; one word covers both.

clue.text: Unacceptable old hat

definitions.meaning: not allowed, as an idea that is ruled not on

explanation.surface: A dated hat that nobody would wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old hat' is an idiom for out of date, not a piece of headwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ruled impossible is not on, and a dated fashion has gone from current favour; one short word covers both.

clue.text: Real comet explodes to become one in tail

indicators.note: an explosion scatters the pieces, so the letters of the two words fly into a new order

explanation.surface: A real comet bursts apart and ends up in its own tail.
explanation.walkthrough: The comet's 'tail' suggests astronomy; here it is the tail end of a queue, where a late arrival stands.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone arriving after the others joins at the back, the tail of a queue.

clue.text: In a passenger-ship, Italian food is for well-trained horses

definitions.note: plural definition for a word also used as a plural of the breed

indicators.note: the food is said to be inside the ship, so it goes within that word

parts.note: a liner is a large passenger ship
pizza is the famous Italian dish

explanation.surface: On an ocean liner, Italian cooking is served to performing horses.
explanation.walkthrough: The Vienna Spanish Riding School's white horses are of this breed, famous for their dressage.
explanation.definitionFit: The Austrian breed of white horses is trained in classical dressage at the Spanish Riding School.

clue.text: Yet girl comes out about 1:50 as an oriental flower

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about, around, the numerals
the letters emerge in a fresh arrangement, so the words are rearranged

parts.note: I is one and L is fifty in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A young woman makes her debut at ten to two, like an Eastern bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes out' turns YET GIRL into TIGERLY, and 'about' places IL (Roman 1 and 50) inside it, between TIGERL and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiger lily is an orange spotted lily native to East Asia.

clue.text: Seamy location

parts.note: seamy suggests sordid, but here it means full of seams, the layers miners dig

explanation.surface: A sordid neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: A mining area where seams of black fuel lie underground.

clue.text: Expression of grief in a reduced state

indicators.note: the state is cut down, its tail end of two letters removed

parts.note: Alaska is the largest US state

explanation.surface: Grief that leaves someone in a sorry, diminished condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced state' reads as a weakened condition, but it is a US state with its last two letters cut.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an interjection voicing sorrow or regret.

clue.text: Some saying mince-pie carries very little weight

indicators.note: the word mince-pie carries some letters inside it

parts.note: a gram is a tiny unit of weight

explanation.surface: A remark that a mince pie hardly weighs anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carries' looks like the pie bearing weight; it signals letters carried within 'mince-pie'.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigram is a short witty saying or pithy remark.

clue.text: Limits achieved by Henley's opening boat-crews

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: eights are rowing crews of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: Records set by the leading rowing crews at the Henley regatta.
explanation.walkthrough: Henley Royal Regatta is a famous English rowing event on the Thames; an eight is a rowing boat with eight oarsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Heights are the utmost points or peaks, the furthest limits reached.

clue.text: Rooftop bower?

parts.note: bower suggests a leafy arbour, but it is one who uses a bow, playing high on a roof as in the musical

explanation.surface: A garden arbour built on top of a house.
explanation.walkthrough: The musical 'Fiddler on the Roof' gives the rooftop; a violin player draws a bow, so is a 'bower'.
explanation.definitionFit: A violinist plays with a bow, and the famous musical puts one on a roof.

clue.text: Nicholas possibly the last character to be carried in a limo?

indicators.note: the letter rides inside the vehicle, so it goes within that word

parts.note: a limousine is a car
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Could Nicholas be the last person to be chauffeured in a limousine?
explanation.walkthrough: Nicholas II was the last Russian emperor, so 'last character' points cleverly both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicholas II was the final Russian emperor, an example of the title.

clue.text: If at early development, this is an improbable romance

indicators.note: development changes a thing's form, so the letters of these words are reshaped

explanation.surface: A love story at an early stage that seems unlikely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' looks like a link word but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanciful story of magic and happy endings, the type of tale nobody expects in real life.

clue.text: The northern fox a sly fellow?

definitions.meaning: in northern English and Scots dialect a ... is a fox

explanation.surface: A northern fox described as a crafty character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'northern' signals a dialect word from Scotland and the north of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A northern dialect word for a fox, which also describes a cunning person.

clue.text: Garland used in Hawaiian isle investiture

indicators.note: the answer is used inside these words, spanning two of them

explanation.surface: A flower garland worn at a ceremony on a Hawaiian island.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hawaiian necklace of flowers given as a welcome is a lei.

clue.text: I ask about what to drink in Japan

indicators.note: turned about, the letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asks what drink to order in Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a variant spelling of sake, the Japanese rice wine.

clue.text: This flier gets us down

parts.note: down suggests depression, but it is the soft feathers this sea bird gives for quilts

explanation.surface: A bird that depresses us.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea bird's soft breast feathers fill quilts, so it supplies people with their down.

clue.text: Painter in a Somerset Maugham story

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a painter
taken as written

explanation.surface: An artist appears in one of Maugham's tales.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, Royal Academician, is a member of London's Royal Academy of Arts and a crossword stand-in for an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Maugham's short story set in Pago Pago, about a missionary and Sadie Thompson, has this weather title.

clue.text: University can put up a number of soldiers

indicators.note: in a down clue putting something up turns it upwards, read backwards

parts.note: a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A college can house a body of troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a verb meaning is able to, but it is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A military unit is a body of soldiers organised together.

clue.text: Family dog's first to be affectionate

parts.note: kin are one's family

indicators.note: the first letter of the word dog's is taken

explanation.surface: The family dog is the first to show affection.
explanation.definitionFit: Kind means warm and gentle, showing affection.

clue.text: Turn down study that takes a year

parts.note: a den is a private room for study
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: Refusing to take a year of study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'study' looks like a verb, but it is the room.
explanation.definitionFit: To refuse a request is to reject or decline it.

clue.text: Day in Rome, taking in old master? They will tell us what we should take!

definitions.text: They will tell us what we should take!

indicators.note: the Latin day takes the painter inside it

parts.note: dies is Latin for day
Titian was the great Venetian old-master painter

explanation.surface: A day in Rome viewing old paintings, followed by advice on what to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take' looks like what you take in a gallery; it means what we should eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Experts on nutrition advise on diet, telling people what foods to eat.
